problem: Prior language-guided and visual navigation methods treat detected landmarks (e.g. curtains, grass) as untraversable obstacles, so no feasible path exists when the goal lies behind a traversable obstacle. Landmark-only extraction from LLMs ignores the verbs/actions (e.g. 'pass through') that determine traversability.
motivation: Robots such as medicine-delivery dogs need real-time human interaction (e.g. from patients in bed) to go where normal planners refuse, such as through curtains. Extracting action-aware attributes from language and feeding them into costmap construction shifts feasibility to the planner and avoids task-specific navigators or extra training data.
key_idea: Use GPT-3.5 to extract landmarks with action-aware traversable/untraversable flags from instructions, ground them with Grounding DINO, and use the boxes to split LiDAR points into traversable (free) and untraversable (lethal) parts for an action-aware costmap plus A* planning.
insight: The verb in the instruction determines an object's traversability, so injecting this attribute into the costmap makes otherwise blocked goals reachable without fine-tuning. Qualitatively, the paper shows that without the action-aware costmap no path is found (simulation and real), while with it the robot passes curtains and grass. There is no quantitative ablation.
method: LLM parsing: GPT-3.5 with two in-context examples outputs (landmark, P) pairs, where P=1 means traversable under the action and P=0 means untraversable.
VLM grounding: Grounding DINO takes the landmark names as a text prompt and outputs bounding boxes {cx,cy,w,h} in the camera image.
LiDAR-to-image projection: 2D LiDAR points are projected to the image via the intrinsic and extrinsic matrices.
Point cloud segmentation: A point is traversable only if all bounding boxes containing it have P=1; overlaps between traversable and untraversable boxes are treated as untraversable for safety.
Action-aware costmap: Traversable points get cost 0 (FREESPACE) and untraversable points get 254 (LETHALSPACE) in a layered costmap that is updated online.
Planning: A* on the costmap yields waypoints. Speech can be transcribed by speech recognition before the LLM.

setting.observation: monocular RGB-D camera image (RealSense D435i) + 2D LiDAR, with a prebuilt SLAM map and goal
setting.action_space: A* waypoints on a costmap executed by a legged robot controller
setting.privileged: prebuilt SLAM global map with manually annotated goal location; the traversable landmark is specified by the human instruction

numbers_note: No quantitative results; only qualitative demonstrations in simulation and real-world figures.
results: Qualitatively, without the action-aware costmap no feasible path exists when the goal is behind a curtain or wall. With it, a Unitree A1 passes 4 different curtains, artificial grass, and a medical-scenario curtain while avoiding chairs and warning signs. No success rates or baselines are reported.
limitations: Purely qualitative evaluation with no success rates, baselines, or ablations
2D LiDAR and bounding-box (not mask) segmentation are coarse; boxes may cover partial objects or include background
Assumes a prebuilt map and the human correctly declaring traversability, with no autonomous judgment of safety
